water.what: Soil moisture. It drains slowly around the clock — even while you're away. Below 20% the plant turns thirsty and health starts to slip; at zero it dries out fast. From 40% up, health recovers on its own.
water.how: Press Water for a pour from the rain barrel — carnivorous plants insist on rainwater. If the barrel runs dry, tap water works in a pinch, but the limescale costs a little health.

nutrition.what: How well fed the plant is. Insects are a bonus meal, not dinner — light and water keep it alive — but a full belly speeds growth by up to half.
nutrition.how: Snappy species eat when you tap a trap with an insect close by. The others take dried flies with the Feed button every few hours — and the sundew's sticky leaves catch tiny prey all by themselves.

health.what: The plant's overall condition. It slips while the soil is dry (or the air, for tropical species) and recovers by itself once water is topped up. At 15% the plant wilts; it perks back up at 40%. Only hard mode lets a plant die for good.
health.how: Keep water comfortably topped up, mist the humidity lovers, and grant a winter rest to species that need one. A wilted plant pauses growing and snapping until it recovers.

humidity.what: Air moisture — only tropical species mind it. Below 25% the dry air chips away at health, and below 40% growth slows down.
humidity.how: Give the plant a misting now and then. The greenhouse holds moisture, so humidity drains at half pace in there.

growth.what: Progress toward the next stage, from seedling all the way to a mature plant. Growth runs on light and water, with a well-fed bonus of up to +50%. A wilted or bone-dry plant stops growing.
growth.how: Park the plant in the sunniest spot it likes, keep the water up and the belly full. The status line guesses when the next stage arrives with the care you're giving.

barrel.what: Your stash of collected rainwater — the only water carnivorous plants truly love. It refills on its own whenever it rains.
barrel.how: Every watering draws from the barrel. If it runs low, wait for rain — or fall back on tap water, which always works but costs a little health in limescale.

dewdrops.what: The game's currency. Daily care, quests, achievements, pulled weeds, petting, perfect pours and blooms all pay out dewdrops.
dewdrops.how: Spend them in the shop on new species, gear like the grow light and the greenhouse, and cosy decor for the room.

dionaea.name: Venus flytrap
dionaea.facts: Each trap can only snap shut a few times before it withers — the plant grows new ones. It photosynthesizes like any plant; insects are a bonus meal, not dinner. Native to a tiny patch of the Carolinas, and it truly needs a cold winter rest.

drosera.name: Sundew
drosera.facts: Its leaves glisten with sticky droplets that catch tiny insects all by themselves — the leaf slowly curls around the catch. One of the most forgiving carnivorous plants to keep, and it blooms readily on a sunny sill.

nepenthes.name: Tropical pitcher plant
nepenthes.facts: Grows hanging pitchers of digestive fluid that insects tumble into. A true tropical: it never sleeps in winter but craves humid air — mist it often and keep it warm.

sarracenia.name: Trumpet pitcher
sarracenia.facts: Tall trumpet-shaped leaves lure insects with nectar along the rim; once inside, downward hairs stop the way back. Wants blazing sun all summer and a proper cold dormancy all winter.

b52.name: B52
b52.facts: A celebrated giant among flytraps — its traps grow well past five centimetres, among the largest ever raised. The name was simply the grower's bench label, not the bomber.

red-dragon.name: Red Dragon
red-dragon.facts: An all-red cultivar — 'Akai Ryū' is Japanese for red dragon. The burgundy comes from anthocyanin, the same pigment that reddens autumn leaves, and it deepens in strong light.

justina.name: Justina Davis
justina.facts: Stays entirely green even in blazing sun — a natural variant that makes no red pigment at all. Named after the wife of the colonial governor who wrote the first known description of the Venus flytrap.

onboarding.welcome1: Flytrap Keeper is a calm, real-time care game. Your carnivorous plant lives on while you're away — drop by a few times a day, tend to it, and watch it grow from seedling to bloom.
onboarding.tip1: Water it from the rain barrel. Tap water works, but the limescale hurts.
onboarding.tip2: Each trap can only snap a few times before it withers — a new one grows back.
onboarding.tip3: Catching insects is a tasty bonus. Light and water are what keep it alive.
onboarding.packetDesc: The classic. Snappy jaws, a big appetite, and a love of bright light.
